assays.assay_name: Head Twitch Response (with concurrent open-field locomotor activity)
assays.assay_description: Single 30-min session in open field chambers (Coulbourn photobeam arrays with cylindrical inserts and custom floor panels for video). Mice received s.c. drug or vehicle after a 5-min arena acclimation and baseline temperature reading; total HTR events (scored from video with CleverSys software), total distance traveled (photobeams) and change in body temperature (transponder) were measured over the session, with HTR and locomotor time-courses plotted across the session.

application_type.evidence: All drugs were dissolved in 0.9% saline and administered subcutaneously (s.c.)

setup_habituation.evidence: Each test session started with a short 5 min period of acclimation to the testing arenas, followed by baseline temperature recording.

setup_restrain.evidence: Mice were ... returned to the test chambers for a 30 min session; locomotor activity was recorded continuously using open field chambers (freely moving, no restraint described).

food_restriction.evidence: ad libitum access to food and water [home cage]; the open field test chambers contained no food.

water_restriction.evidence: ad libitum access to food and water [home cage]; no water source described in the test chambers.

time_to_assay.evidence: Mice were next injected s.c. with appropriate doses of test drug or vehicle and returned to the test chambers for a 30 min session.

sample_size.evidence: 24 total with 12 male and 12 female mice/drug; Dose-response curves for effects on the HTR (n = 5-6 mice/dose)

outcomes.summary: Aside from the bulky N-n-butyl, N-tert-butyl and N-cyclohexyl analogues, all norpsilocin analogues produced dose-related increases in head twitches with inverted U-shaped dose-response curves (ED50 = 1.1-3.3 mg/kg; Emax = 26-77 HTR events/30 min), ~10-fold less potent than psilocin. Time-courses differed between compounds (4-HO-NPT, 4-HO-NALT and 4-HO-NBnT peaked at 5-15 min; 4-HO-NET and 4-HO-NiPT peaked at 15-25 min). Only 4-HO-NET, 4-HO-NPT, 4-HO-NnBT and 4-HO-NBnT significantly reduced total locomotor activity, at doses ~10-fold above HTR-active doses (hypothermia also occurred at 10 and 30 mg/kg).
outcomes.statistics: One-way ANOVA with Dunnett's posthoc test (p < 0.05); ED50 (95% CI) mg/kg s.c.: 4-HO-NET 1.4 (0.9-2.4), 4-HO-NPT 2.9 (2.7-3.1), 4-HO-NALT 1.1 (0.9-1.3), 4-HO-NiPT 3.3 (2.6-4.4), 4-HO-NBnT 1.2 (1.0-1.5); 4-HO-NnBT, 4-HO-NtBT, 4-HO-NcHT >30. Emax (HTR events/30 min): 39.8, 52.1, 76.6, 27.5, 26.1 respectively.
outcomes.evidence: Aside from the bulky N-butyl and N-cyclohexyl substitutions, all compounds produced dose-related increases in HTRs vs vehicle controls (Figure 3, Figure S1, Table S1), with dose-response curves exhibiting the typical inverted U shape; ... only half of the compounds significantly reduced locomotor activity over the test session.

B1_num_measures.evidence: Mean total number of HTRs over the 30 min session, change in body temperature from pre to post session (Δ°C), and total distance traveled (cm) ... were evaluated (HTR count and distance traveled are the behavioural measures).

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: (A) Dose-response curves for effects on the HTR and representative time-course plots for HTR activity of (B) 4-HO-NET, (C) 4-HO-NPT, and (D) 4-HO-NALT; peak effects within 5-15 min ... up to 15-25 min post drug administration.

B3_sequential_structure.evidence: No analysis of behavioural transitions, sequences or bout microstructure is reported.

B4_ethological.evidence: Measures are head-twitch response and locomotor distance, both explicitly non-ethological per the rubric.

B5_social.evidence: Mice were tested individually in open field chambers; no social construct measured.

B6_cognitive.evidence: No learning, memory or cognitive flexibility component in the HTR/locomotor session.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: HTR quantified via a commercially available software platform (Clever Sys Inc.) and locomotion via photobeam arrays — both on the SCORE-0 list.

B8_multivariate.evidence: Data analysed with one-way ANOVA and nonlinear regression; no PCA/clustering of behavioural features.

judge_notes: Merged the candidates' separate 'Head Twitch Response' and 'Locomotor Activity (Open Field)' entries into ONE assay: HTR, distance traveled and body temperature were all collected simultaneously within the same single 30-min session in the same open field chamber under the same protocol; the locomotor measure is an additional outcome variable of that session (captured in B1 = 2-3 measures), not a separate behavioural test.
Body temperature change is a purely physiological measure and was excluded from the B1 behavioural measure count (HTR events + distance traveled = 2 behavioural measures).
B7 scored 0: HTR was quantified with CleverSys software and locomotion with Coulbourn photobeam arrays — both explicitly on the rubric's SCORE-0 list.

Dosing: the main text states only the two highest doses (10 and 30 mg/kg) and ED50 values; the full dose series is in Supporting Information (not visible), so doses_mg_per_kg was limited to [10, 30] rather than inheriting deepseek's unsupported '1, 3, 10, 30 mg/kg'. Psilocin and norpsilocin HTR data are from a previously published report, so they are not listed as compounds dosed in this study.

setup_habituation retained as 'yes' (modal) because the 5-min arena acclimation occurred before injection and before data collection, though the paper frames it as the start of the test session (confidence lowered to medium).
D4 scored 0: the only pre-drug recording was body temperature (physiological), not behaviour.
n_total reported as 24 (mice per drug) per the Methods statement; the smallest cell n is 5 ('n = 5-6 mice/dose').
